name: IL-15
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's 20-point Republican partisan lean makes this deeply red territory
Incumbent Mary Miller holds a roughly 12-to-1 cash advantage over Jennifer Todd
Prediction markets price Miller at about 96 percent to win
No polls or expert ratings exist; the Democratic-leaning environment only modestly narrows the gap
model.rationale: The seat's 20-point Republican lean, Miller's incumbency and dominant fundraising edge, and markets pricing her near-certain re-election leave no evidence of a competitive race; the favorable national environment for Democrats shaves a few points off the margin but nowhere near enough to matter.
model.watch: A major scandal involving Miller or a sudden influx of Democratic outside spending could tighten the race, though nothing currently signals either.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Illinois's 15th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the state, with a partisan lean of roughly 20 points toward the GOP. Republican incumbent Mary Miller is seeking re-election and holds an overwhelming financial advantage, having raised about $1.3 million with $810,000 on hand, while Democrat Jennifer Todd has raised roughly $113,000 with $31,000 available. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets put Miller's chances at about 96 percent.

The Democratic-favorable national environment trims a few points off the Republican margin but leaves the seat firmly in GOP hands. With no sign of a competitive race developing, Miller is positioned to win re-election by a wide double-digit margin.
